title: An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Core arrives
scenes.purpose: Set up the slate studio stage and drop the copper core onto its plinth.
visuals: Dark slate (#303C40) stage with a stationary sage key-light lift behind the plinth
Copper metal core sphere drops 1.4 units with a back-ease settle onto the slate plinth with its copper inlay ring
Camera starts on a raised three-quarter view about 30° off axis

beats.development: Core scales up and settles onto the plinth; its contact shadow fades in; the camera begins its weighted orbit.

scenes.title: Assembly
scenes.purpose: Show the idea connecting: rods extend and four satin nodes seat on them.
visuals: Four dark metal rods grow out of the core in sequence
Satin sage nodes appear above and outside their sockets, then a baked XPBD compliant attachment pulls them in until they clack against the rod-length contact
Lower nodes come to rest on the floor with contact shadows

beats.development: Upper-left and upper-right nodes seat on their rods; the rods swing to follow each incoming node.
The lower-left and lower-right nodes seat; the headline begins rising in line by line.

scenes.title: Settle and read
scenes.purpose: Finish the camera settle, complete the copy and hold the readable system.
visuals: Camera completes its dolly to the near-front 17° view by 2.3s
Nodes locked exactly in their seats by 2.5s
Copy column complete on the flat slate stage

beats.development: The last headline lines and the body copy reveal while the camera settles.
captions: One copper core, four satin nodes,
a single key light from upper left.

beats.development: Static hold on the complete assembled scene and copy.

findings: Every object is in place and all copy is fully opaque by 2.55s, inside the 2.7s requirement.
The motion is substantial: the camera orbit, the core drop, rod growth and node travel cover most of the left 60% of the frame.
justifiedHolds: 2.6–3.0s: a 0.4s final hold so the complete headline and body can be read on a 3s card.

notes: Silent preview: no music, effects or voice.

Background refresh: a cool slate studio stage replaces the earlier warm cream canvas, following the background review's dark-stage lessons (sources 2 and 3) and the fog-depth lesson (source 1). No source subject, wording or branding is reused.

No reviewed preview recipes were supplied (tech.preview_recipes is absent), so the preview demonstrates the primary style: real 3D geometry, a coherent key light, contact shadows and a weighted assembly.
